access_notes.value: API access requires a paid plan: Standard (200 calls/min, no reporting endpoints), Plus, or Pro (all endpoints). The Free plan excludes API and integrations. rate_limits.value: Inbox API: Standard up to 200 calls/min, Plus up to 400 calls/min, Pro up to 800 calls/min; write requests and v3 search calls count as 2 requests. Docs API: 2,000 requests/10 min (1 site), 3,000 (2 sites), 4,000 (3+ sites).

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: While we won’t introduce any breaking changes, we plan on adding new features and new endpoints over time. Our changelog can be monitored to see when and how the API was updated.

verdict_reason: Help Scout documents broad read-write APIs (Inbox API 2.0, Docs API, Chat API, webhooks) plus a vendor-operated MCP server, so the integration surface is substantial. However, credentials are gated by plan tier: 'The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations,' and API access starts on paid Standard/Plus/Pro plans. No sales contact or partner review is required, so it is moderate rather than hard.
main_blocker: Paid Help Scout plan required for API access
open_questions: Whether OAuth scopes/permissions are documented for the Inbox API is not evidenced; only user-role permissions are described (e.g., the Docs API key permission 'Docs: Create new, edit settings & Collections').
No documented sandbox or test environment was found in the fetched pages; confirm whether test accounts/mailboxes are available.
Official SDKs beyond PHP may exist, but the API clients page was not fetched; only the PHP SDK is evidenced as vendor-maintained.
Endpoint/resource count for Inbox API 2.0 is not stated in the fetched pages, so api_breadth is qualitative.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found in the provided evidence (MCP registry results: none); a dedicated registry search may be needed.
api_type 'REST' is inferred from documented HTTP verbs and endpoint structure; no fetched page explicitly labels the API as REST.
Legacy Mailbox API 1.0 deprecation (November 20, 2019) appeared only in a search snippet, not in a fetched source, so it was excluded from the versioning claim.
